key_insight: This paper introduces a hierarchical continuous diffusion language model that aims to preserve token dependencies during parallel decoding. By combining shared continuous-state denoising with hierarchical structure, it seeks to improve global consistency beyond standard discrete diffusion methods.
problem_solved: It addresses the bottleneck in diffusion-based language generation where tokens decoded in parallel are sampled independently, which breaks dependencies and can hurt coherence and constraint satisfaction.
method: Use a continuous diffusion formulation to denoise a shared latent state rather than independently sampling tokens.
Introduce a hierarchical structure so the model can capture both coarse global context and finer token-level details.
Preserve statistical dependencies among jointly decoded tokens to improve bidirectional reasoning and global constraint handling.
impact: This matters because it offers a path toward more coherent, globally consistent text generation without relying on purely autoregressive decoding. For practitioners, it could improve tasks like constrained generation, editing, and reasoning-heavy language modeling.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of autoregressive, discrete diffusion, and hierarchical continuous diffusion decoding
